summary: The billing migration for 410,000 accounts went live with a rehearsal abandoned after an 11-hour data-load overrun, 14 open defects (two high), and a go decision on Sunday night. Since then the portal has had repeated outages, 4,200 customers were double-debited (€612,000), and call waits have reached 47 minutes. Rollback is no longer possible, and the 1 December billing run for 180,000 accounts and the vendor's exit on 30 November are both approaching.

signals.observation: Cutover rehearsal coverage was incomplete: only one of three planned rehearsals finished, and the second was abandoned partway.
signals.evidence: "The plan called for three full cutover rehearsals. One was completed, and the second was abandoned halfway when the data load overran by 11 hours."

signals.observation: The go decision was taken with known open defects, including high-severity ones.
signals.evidence: "the go/no-go call approved the cutover with 14 open defects, two of them rated high."

signals.observation: The customer portal failed for a full day and then repeatedly after go-live.
signals.evidence: "The customer portal was down for nine hours on Monday. Three more outages of two to three hours followed during the week"

signals.observation: The outages have a known technical cause that is not yet fixed.
signals.evidence: "traced to database connection limits under peak load."

signals.observation: Customers were billed incorrectly on a large scale, with direct financial impact.
signals.evidence: "4,200 customers were debited twice, a total of €612,000."

signals.observation: Remediation depends on manual work that cannot keep up with the backlog.
signals.evidence: "Refunds are being processed by hand at about 300 a day."

signals.observation: Customer service capacity is badly strained.
signals.evidence: "Call volume tripled to 14,000 calls a day, with average waits of 47 minutes."

signals.observation: Rollback to the old system is no longer possible, removing the fallback option.
signals.evidence: "Rollback is no longer possible because meter reads since Monday exist only in the new platform."

signals.observation: A regulatory deadline and a large billing run are at risk.
signals.evidence: "The energy regulator wants an incident report within ten working days" and "The next monthly billing run, for 180,000 accounts, is due on 1 December."

signals.observation: Vendor support ends before the billing run and before stabilisation is likely to be complete.
signals.evidence: "under the contract the vendor’s six-person hypercare team leaves on 30 November."

things_to_watch: Exact date the regulator's ten-working-day deadline falls on and who owns the incident report
Current status and owner of the 14 open defects, especially the two high-severity ones
Whether the database connection limit fix is scheduled and tested before the 1 December run
Total refunds completed versus outstanding and the remaining duplicate-debit population
Plan and funding for handling the 1 December billing run for 180,000 accounts
Whether a post-30 November support arrangement with the vendor is possible
Named accountable executive and decision owner for further go/no-go or rollback-related calls
Whether meter read data since Monday has a validated backup or reconciliation route
